title: oncall-signal-noise-ecc-patterns-and-suspected-psu-glitch-notes-2029-02-14
content:
Purpose
-----
Quick capture of the nightshift on-call observations (Feb 14–15), an early hypothesis connecting clustered ECC surges with transient PSU voltage events on rack-07, and a runnable checklist to help reproduce/triage in lab. This is rough — notes for the team before a proper postmortem.

Executive summary
-----------------
- Symptom: intermittent correctable ECC spikes on multiple cards in rack-07 between 23:10 and 01:05 local. Some nodes then experienced nvlink flapping and one kernel panic.
- Immediate impact: 3 hosts had degraded throughput (retries and elevated tail latencies), 1 host rebooted after kernel panic; no customer data loss observed.
- Leading hypothesis: ECC bursts coincide with short, sub-second dips on the 12V GPU rail from a failing PSU or rack-level power conditioner; thermal changes and NVLink retraining amplify error surface and eventually trigger driver-level instability.
- Confidence: low->medium (correlation across telemetry + correlated PDUs events, but need hardware capture).

Observed timeline (raw)
----------------------
- 2029-02-14 22:58: alerted by autoscaler: node gpu-node-07b high correctable-ecc-rate (threshold 50/min).
- 2029-02-14 23:03: oncall Slack: spike continues, PV 12V PDU event logged (pdu-07-A transient drop 23:02:58).
- 2029-02-14 23:10–23:20: burst of ECC on 07b, 07c, 07d; NVLink counters (link-flaps) rose on 07c at 23:14.
- 2029-02-14 23:48: kernel oops on 07d; host froze and auto-rebooted via watchdog.
- 2029-02-15 00:05: returns to baseline for ~30m; then smaller spikes 00:40 and 00:59 aligned with more PDU transient logs.
- 2029-02-15 01:06: no further events; monitoring shows small residual ECC activity for 2 hours.

Diagnostics collected
---------------------
- Telemetry captured: ECC_correctable_count (per-GPU), nvlink_error_count, gpu-temp, fan-speed, host-power-watts, pdu-event-log.
- Exported traces: syslogs and kernel oops from 07d (attached to ticket SRE-4578).
- Hardware: vendor BMC logs for the affected hosts (07b-d) show PDU drop events and alerted on redundant-PSU imbalance on 07c.
- Quick stats: aggregated over the hour, affected GPUs saw 10–100x normal correctable-ECC rate.

Interesting correlations and patterns
-----------------------------------
- ECC spikes are short-lived (10–60s), often in bursts, and not steady degradation.
- Temperature delta: small - spikes happened during times when GPU temp rose ~2–3°C over 30s (likely due to transient power changes).
- NVLink: link retrain counts increase shortly after ECC bursts; suggests link negotiation after memory error detection.
- PSU/PDU: PDU event timestamps match top-percentile ECC bursts within <2s in 6/7 observed bursts.
- Host-level: only when ECC bursts coincide with nvlink flaps or when other GPUs in same host show simultaneous ECC does a kernel panic occur.

Hypotheses (short form)
-----------------------
1) Primary: intermittent PSU voltage droop on 12V rail -> momentary undervoltage -> increased ECC correctable errors -> NVLink retrain -> driver stack hit race -> kernel panic on unlucky path. (Mechanism plausible; matches PDU logs.)
2) Alternative: localized EMI/grounding issue on rack-07 (less likely; would expect broader device noise and switch logs).
3) Software-only: recent driver build exposes latent race when ECC counters spike (possible; check driver rollouts).

Immediate mitigations applied
---------------------------
- Isolated rack-07 workloads: shifted critical serving traffic to other racks, reduced load on affected hosts (automated via placement policy).
- Power ops: asked on-call infra to throttle PDU/redistribute phase loads and to swap in known-good PSU on 07c during maintenance window.
- Monitoring: lowered ECC alert threshold temporarily and enabled an automated runbook that cycles the GPU driver only when ECC rate > 500/min for >60s (avoid noisy flaps).

Short checklist to reproduce in lab (priority tasks)
---------------------------------------------------
- Hardware setup: replicate with two GPUs connected via NVLink on the same host, ideally same model/firmware. Put a programmable power supply inline with 12V rail to simulate short droops.
- Software: load kernel module and driver version matching production (driver X.Y.Z) and run memory stress (memtest for gpus or cudamemtest equivalent) while toggling power.
- Observe: ECC counters, nvlink retrain counters, driver logs for traces and backtraces.
- Acceptance criteria: reproduces ECC burst + nvlink retrain; if kernel panic reproducible, capture console serial logs + kdump.

Runbook draft (triage steps for oncall)
--------------------------------------
1) Triage start (first alert): collect these before doing anything destructive:
   - Identify host(s): kubectl get nodes --selector=gpu=true -o wide (identify node name and rack tag).
   - Quick telemetry snapshot (last 15m):
     PromQL: increases(ECC_correctable_total{host="gpu-node-07b"}[15m]) by (gpu)
     PromQL: increase(nvlink_retrain_total{host="gpu-node-07b"}[15m])
   - Check PDU and BMC: fetch pdu logs for rack (pductl show events --rack rack-07 --since 1h) and bmc journal.

2) If PDU/BMC shows events within ±5s of ECC spike: escalate to hardware ops (pager). Include timestamp and attach outage window.

3) If no PDU events: collect driver logs and rundriver level health check:
   - dmesg | tail -n 200 | grep -i -E "ecc|nvlink|gpu|nvrm|oops"
   - nvmlDeviceGetMemoryErrorStats or nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PERF
   - capture gdb backtrace if kernel oops present (follow SRE kdump playbook).

4) Short-term mitigation: cordon node and drain non-critical pods; consider driver reload:
   - systemctl stop redwood-gpu-service
   - modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia
   - modprobe nvidia nvidia_uvm (only if safe and after confirming no running inference jobs)

5) If NVLink flaps persist after driver reload -> enforce physical migration of pods to other hosts and schedule urgent hardware replacement.

Data collection spec (for postmortem)
------------------------------------
- Telemetry windows: capture continuous metrics with 1s granularity for the 10 minute window surrounding each ECC burst (ECC counts, nvlink retrain, gpu temp, fan, host power, PDU voltage rails).
- Logs: persist kernel oops, dmesg, journalctl -k, BMC logs, PDU event exports.
- Hardware: keep suspect PSU and swap logs (serials), capture FRU data.

Open questions (to resolve in follow-ups)
----------------------------------------
- Can we prove causal link between 12V micro-dips and ECC increases, or is correlation a red herring? Need lab reproducibility.
- Driver path: is there an unprotected code path that will oops on concurrent ECC notifications + nvlink retrain? Ask driver team for audit of recent commits.
- Why are only some hosts in rack-07 affected (07b-d) while 07a is fine? Differences in PSU serials, riser orientation, or workload patterns?

Action items (owners)
---------------------
- Priya: coordinate lab reproduction with hw bench and schedule PSU injection test (due 2029-02-20).
- Ethan: collect high-resolution telemetry export and upload to SRE storage (S3 link in SRE-4578) (due 2029-02-17).
- Zoe: open hardware ticket with datacenter ops to replace suspect PSU on 07c and request PDU-level power conditioning check (ticket DC-811) (due ASAP).
- Luca: audit driver rollouts for last 30 days and flag any commits touching nvlink or ECC handling (due 2029-02-18).

Notes to self / rough follow-ups
-------------------------------
- Consider adding a short-lived automation: if ECC spikes co-occur with PDU events, temporarily quiesce GPU workloads automatically (instead of only throttling).
- We should expose NVLink retrain rates in the daily SRE digest and create a per-rack health radar.
- Keep an eye on similar patterns in other racks — the current pattern may propagate as PSU inventory ages.

Appendix: useful commands and PromQL examples
--------------------------------------------
- List ECC increases across cluster (last 1h):
  sum by (host) (increase(ECC_correctable_total[1h])) | sort_desc
- NVLink retrain spike detection (alert idea):
  increase(nvlink_retrain_total[5m]) > 3 and increase(ECC_correctable_total[5m]) > 100
- PDU query (example, replace with actual pductl):
  pductl tail --rack rack-07 --since 2h | grep -i "drop\|voltage\|fault"

End quick notes. Will clean and expand into a full postmortem if we get reproducible results in the lab. If anyone sees a glaring omission, drop a note here or ping oncall.
